picks.rationale: A full 135-min AI-generated feature made for five figures is a concrete shock to how filmmakers weigh budgets and generative-video pipelines — high actionability, novel, credible trade outlet.
picks.excerpt: Fountain O unveiled 'Odysseus: The Fall,' a 135-minute AI-generated retelling of Homer's epic by director Ash Koosha, made for a mid-five-figure budget using Kling after OpenAI shuttered Sora. It launches to piggyback on Christopher Nolan's $250M traditional adaptation, dramatizing how generative video collapses feature-film budgets and workflows.

picks.rationale: A funded festival competition that explicitly permits AI in pitches but mandates section-by-section disclosure — an actionable template for how filmmakers submit AI-assisted work now.
picks.excerpt: Short Shorts Film Festival & Asia opened a pitch competition offering ¥10 million in production funding for a winning short drama, permitting generative AI in pitch materials but requiring filmmakers to disclose exactly which sections used AI. A window into how major festivals are writing AI-disclosure rules into creative submissions.

picks.rationale: A synthetic performer headlining a feature is a live escalation of the AI-casting/likeness fight that directly shapes how the industry treats performers — novel and consequential.
picks.excerpt: The AI-generated 'actress' Tilly Norwood is reportedly set to headline a feature called 'Misaligned' from Particle6 Productions — a 'coming-of-age story infused with existential AI chaos' set in the 'Tillyverse.' The move escalates the synthetic-performer fight (SAG-AFTRA: 'not an actor'), a live test of AI likeness/casting in narrative film.
